title: -ir and -re verbs
description: Conjugate finir-, partir-, ouvrir- and vendre-type verbs in the present.
rule: Regular -ir verbs like finir, choisir and réussir take -is, -is, -it in the singular and add -iss- before the plural endings: nous finissons, vous finissez, ils finissent. Verbs like partir, sortir, dormir and servir drop the last consonant of the stem in the singular (je pars, tu dors, il sert) and keep it in the plural with -ons, -ez, -ent (nous partons, ils dorment), never with -iss-. Ouvrir, offrir and découvrir end in -ir but take the -er endings: j’ouvre, tu offres, il découvre, nous ouvrons, ils ouvrent. Regular -re verbs like vendre, attendre, entendre, répondre and perdre keep their d and take -s, -s, no ending, -ons, -ez, -ent: je vends, il attend, nous répondons, ils perdent. So before conjugating an -ir verb, decide which of the three families it belongs to.
example: Je finis à cinq heures et je pars à six heures. · Nous ouvrons la fenêtre. · Il attend le bus.
aside: In il attend and elle répond, the final d is silent. The il form of these -dre verbs never adds a -t: il attend, not il attendt.

exercises.hint: Remove -ir from finir. Which singular ending goes with je?
exercises.feedback: Remove -ir and add the singular ending.

exercises.hint: The tu form is the same as the je form.
exercises.feedback: Singular finir-type verbs end in -is, -is, -it.

exercises.hint: Match the ending to elle. Finir-type verbs do not use the same ending for je and elle.
exercises.feedback: Réussis goes with je or tu.

exercises.hint: The ending for il is different from the ending for je.
exercises.feedback: Il forms of finir-type verbs end in -t.

exercises.hint: Choisir is a finir-type verb.
exercises.feedback: Use the je ending -is.
exercises.explanation: Je choisis la robe rouge: chois- + -is.

exercises.hint: Match the ending to il. Finir-type verbs use a different ending for il than for je and tu.
exercises.feedback: One verb tile is the je/tu form.

exercises.hint: In the plural, finir-type verbs add a syllable before the ending.
exercises.feedback: Plural forms of finir have -iss-.

exercises.hint: The plural forms of choisir add -iss-.
exercises.feedback: Put -iss- before the nous ending.

exercises.source: Vous ____ vos devoirs avant le dîner.
exercises.hint: Plural finir forms have a double s.
exercises.feedback: Look for -iss- and the vous ending.

exercises.instruction: Change il to ils and adjust the verb.
exercises.hint: Plural finir-type forms add -iss-.
exercises.feedback: Ils réussit is not enough: the plural stem is longer.

exercises.hint: Elles needs the long plural stem.
exercises.feedback: Plural finir forms have -iss-.

exercises.hint: Finir is not an -er verb.
exercises.feedback: The plural of finir needs -iss-.

exercises.hint: Dormir drops a consonant in the singular.
exercises.feedback: Remove the m as well as -ir, then add -s.
exercises.explanation: Je dors: the m of dorm- disappears in the singular.

exercises.source: Il ____ avec ses amis ce soir.
exercises.hint: Sortir is like partir, not like finir.
exercises.feedback: The singular stem drops the t, then il adds -t back as its ending.

exercises.hint: Partir drops its t in the singular.
exercises.feedback: The tu ending is -s.

exercises.hint: In the singular, dormir loses a letter of its stem.
exercises.feedback: Drop the m.
exercises.explanation: Je dors: dormir loses its m in the singular.

exercises.hint: Dormir drops its m in the singular.
exercises.feedback: The il/elle ending of this family is -t.

exercises.hint: Partir drops its t in the singular. Which ending goes with je?
exercises.feedback: One verb tile is the il form.

exercises.hint: In the plural, the full stem comes back.
exercises.feedback: Partir-type verbs never take -iss-.

exercises.hint: The m comes back in the plural.
exercises.feedback: Use the full stem and the ils ending.

exercises.source: Ils ____ du cinéma à dix heures.
exercises.hint: Sortir keeps its t in the plural and does not add -iss-.
exercises.feedback: This family takes -ent in the ils form, with no extra syllable.

exercises.instruction: Change il to ils and adjust the verb.
exercises.hint: The v of servir comes back in the plural.
exercises.feedback: Use the full stem serv- with the ils ending.

exercises.instruction: Translate into French, using nous and partir.
exercises.hint: In the plural, partir keeps its t.
exercises.feedback: Use the full stem and the nous ending.

exercises.hint: Dormir is not a finir-type verb.
exercises.feedback: This family never adds -iss-.

alternatives.message: The verb form is right, but je becomes j’ before a vowel: j’ouvre.

exercises.hint: Ouvrir takes the endings of parler. Watch the elision.
exercises.feedback: Ouvrir looks like an -ir verb but uses -er endings.
exercises.explanation: J’ouvre: ouvr- + -e, and je becomes j’.

exercises.source: Tu ____ des fleurs à ta mère ?
exercises.hint: Offrir takes the same endings as parler.
exercises.feedback: Use the -er ending for tu.

exercises.hint: Ouvrir behaves like an -er verb in the present.
exercises.feedback: Use the il ending of -er verbs.

exercises.hint: Découvrir is not a finir-type verb.
exercises.feedback: Use the -er ending for nous, without -iss-.

exercises.instruction: Change elle to elles and adjust the verb.
exercises.hint: Offrir takes the -er ending for elles.
exercises.feedback: Add the silent plural ending.

exercises.hint: Ouvrir takes -er endings, and je changes before a vowel.
exercises.feedback: The je form ends in -e.

exercises.hint: Keep the stem attend-. What does an -re verb add for il?
exercises.feedback: Keep the d and add nothing.
exercises.explanation: Il attend: attend- with no ending, and no -t.

exercises.hint: Keep the d and add the je ending.
exercises.feedback: The je ending of -re verbs is -s.

exercises.hint: Répondre is a regular -re verb. Its stem ends in d.
exercises.feedback: Nothing is added after the d.
exercises.explanation: Elle répond: répond- with no ending.

exercises.hint: Perdre is a regular -re verb.
exercises.feedback: Use the stem perd- and the nous ending, without -iss-.

exercises.hint: The stem of entendre ends in d, and it stays.
exercises.feedback: The il form keeps the d and adds nothing.
exercises.explanation: Il entend: entend- with no ending.

exercises.source: They (masculine) are waiting for the train.
exercises.hint: Attendre already means “wait for”.
exercises.feedback: Use the ils form of attendre and no word for “for”.
exercises.explanation: Ils attendent le train: attend- + -ent, with a direct object.

exercises.source: You are selling your car. (to a friend)
exercises.hint: Match the verb tile to tu, not to il.
exercises.feedback: One verb tile is the il form.

exercises.instruction: Choose the right form of servir.
exercises.source: Ils ____ le dîner à sept heures.
exercises.hint: Servir belongs to the partir family.
exercises.feedback: Partir-type verbs do not add -iss-.
exercises.explanation: Ils servent: servir is a partir-type verb.

exercises.instruction: Choose the right form of choisir.
exercises.hint: Choisir belongs to the finir family.
exercises.feedback: Finir-type verbs add -iss- in the plural.
exercises.explanation: Vous choisissez: choisir is a finir-type verb.

exercises.source: Mes chats ____ et mes enfants finissent leurs devoirs.
exercises.hint: Finissent is a finir-type form. Is dormir in the same family?
exercises.feedback: Dormir does not take -iss-.
exercises.explanation: Mes chats dorment: dormir is a partir-type verb, unlike finir.

exercises.hint: Partir is not in the finir family.
exercises.feedback: Remove the extra syllable.
exercises.explanation: Ils partent: partir-type verbs never add -iss-.

exercises.instruction: Change je to nous in both places and adjust the verbs.
exercises.hint: The two verbs belong to different families.
exercises.feedback: Only one of the verbs adds -iss-.
exercises.explanation: Nous finissons (finir family) et nous partons (partir family).

exercises.hint: Finir and partir belong to different families.
exercises.feedback: Only one of the two verbs takes -iss-.
exercises.explanation: Ils finissent (with -iss-) et ils partent (without). Leaving out the second ils is also correct.
